source_metadata.title: Abacavir-induced liver toxicity
source_metadata.journal: The Brazilian Journal of Infectious Diseases
source_metadata.source_type: case report with retrospective descriptive cohort component

consistency_findings.handling: Preserved the directly reported count as one atom and the recalculated percentage as a separate calculated_from_reported_data atom.

duplicate_review.note: No cross-batch merge was needed because the three-page source was processed as one semantic unit.

schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom model has no dedicated case-report causality-assessment field; the dechallenge was preserved as a qualitative_result atom rather than converted into a formal causality score.
The model has no explicit relation field linking the index case to the retrospective cohort component; assertions were kept separate and share one publication_id.
extraction_limitations: The article is a three-page case report with an uncontrolled retrospective descriptive cohort component; no formal comparator group or inferential statistical analysis is reported.
The article does not provide abacavir/lamivudine/nevirapine doses in the extracted case text; none were inferred.
The article has no main-text figures or tables; quantitative results are reported in prose.
The article does not report an explicit funding statement; no funding atom was created.
The printed discontinuation percentage conflicts with its numerator/denominator, as documented under consistency_findings.
